get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of the account's invoices and debit notes (and advance payments when that feature is enabled), most recent first.

The list supports rich filtering and sorting through the query parameters below.

By default each item contains the invoice header and its client only. Pass `recursive=1` to also receive the nested line items, payments, taxes, documents and custom fields.

Results are paginated (20 per page by default).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to 20. No maximum is enforced — very large values return very large responses.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description:
Association depth. Defaults to 0.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| -1 | Invoice header only |
| 0 | Header + client (default) |
| 1 | Also include line items, payments, taxes, documents and custom fields |

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single **standard invoice** by id, with full nested detail — line items, payments, taxes, documents, custom fields and the client — in one response (no `recursive` flag needed).

Only standard invoices (document type Invoice) are returned here; an id belonging to another document type (estimate, credit note, debit note, refund, …) returns **404 Invoice not found** — use that type's own single-resource endpoint instead.

Requires permission to view the invoice (all-invoices access, or being the invoice's own staff, plus invoice-details access).

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Edit an existing **standard invoice** by id. Send via `PUT /invoices/{id}` (or `POST /invoices/{id}`) with the full invoice payload — submitted line items, payments and custom fields replace the existing ones.

The invoice **cannot be edited** (returns 400 or 404) when it: is on a different branch than it was created on; has a valid (accepted) electronic invoice; has related credit charges, installment agreements or membership/credit renewals; falls in a closed financial period (non-draft); is tied to a closed POS shift; has a received requisition; or is selected in a production plan.

Requires edit permission — all-invoices edit access, or being the invoice's own staff with edit-own access.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates multiple invoices in a single request. The request body is a **JSON array**; each element has the exact same shape as the body of **Add New Invoice** (an object with an `Invoice` member plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.).

Invoices are created **one by one and the operation is not atomic** — if one element fails validation the others are still created. The response is a **JSON array** with one result object per submitted invoice, in the same order as the request. A successful element carries the new invoice `id` and number; a failed element carries an error result with a message, so you must inspect each element to confirm it succeeded.

Per-element fields and defaulting behaviour are identical to **Add New Invoice** — see that endpoint for the full field reference.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Assigns a work order to an existing invoice (or clears the assignment).

Send the target work order ID nested under the `Invoice` object as `work_order_id`. The invoice is identified by the `id` path parameter. To remove an existing assignment, send `work_order_id` as `0` or empty.

The `Invoice` object is required: if it is omitted the request is rejected with `403` and the message `Please send valid work order id`.

Requires permission to edit the invoice. If the Accounting module is enabled, the invoice's date must not fall within a closed financial period, otherwise the request is rejected with `400`.

Work orders are part of the Work Orders feature; assigning an ID is only meaningful when that feature is enabled for your account.

parameters.description: The invoice ID to assign the work order to.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response format extension, e.g. `.json`.

work_order_id.description: The ID of the work order to assign to the invoice. Send `0` (or an empty value) to clear the current assignment. The value is stored as-is, so it should reference an existing work order in your account.

200.description: The work order was assigned to the invoice.

400.description: The invoice date falls within a closed financial period, so it cannot be modified.

validation_errors.description: Present only when field-level validation errors exist.

403.description: Returned either when the authenticated user lacks permission to edit the invoice (message `Forbidden`), or when the request body is missing the `Invoice` object / work order ID (message `Please send valid work order id`).

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns the account's **active** shipping options — the named delivery methods (each with a fee and an optional tax) that can be applied to invoices.

Notes:

- Only active shipping options are returned; disabled or removed ones are omitted.
- This endpoint is **not paginated** — every active shipping option is returned in a single `data` array, and `page` / `limit` query parameters are ignored.
- It takes no query parameters and no request body.
- Each item exposes `tax_id` as a plain identifier; the related tax record is not embedded.

Requires a valid bearer token; no additional permission is needed.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response format suffix, e.g. `.json`.

data.description: All active shipping options. This list is not paginated.

id.description: Unique identifier of the shipping option.

name.description: Display name of the shipping option (the delivery method shown to clients).

fees.description: Shipping fee charged for this option, returned as a decimal string.

tax_id.description: Identifier of the tax applied to this option's fee, or `null` when no tax applies. The tax record itself is not embedded.

display_order.description: Position used when ordering shipping options for display.

status.description:
Whether the shipping option is active. Only active options are returned by this endpoint.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Inactive |
| 1 | Active |

description.description: Optional free-text description of the shipping option.

created.description: Time the shipping option was created.

modified.description: Time the shipping option was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Always `null` for options returned by this endpoint.

403.description: The account's subscription has expired.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns the configuration for the **currently open POS shift session** — the data a point-of-sale client needs to bootstrap a session: the active language and default payment method, the session's branch and store, the cashier, cash-in/cash-out links, and a set of capability and feature flags derived from your permissions and account settings.

The session is identified by the open shift bound to your authenticated session, or by the `Posshift` request header carrying the POS shift session id when no session binding exists.

Returns **200** only when the shift is open and you are allowed to access it (you opened it and may open your own sessions, or you may open all sessions). Some members of `Shift` appear only when the related feature is enabled — the embedded-barcode lengths when embedded barcodes are configured, and the insurance members when the Insurance feature is active.

parameters.description: Response format extension, e.g. `.json`.

cash_out_url.description: Link to record a cash-out movement for this session.

can_add_discount.description: Whether the cashier may add a discount at point of sale.

check_offers.description: Whether active offers exist and should be evaluated at point of sale.

share_products.description: Whether products are shared across branches.
